title: Simple residue-field extension: Hilbert--Samuel comparison and equality of standard degrees
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $(R,\mathfrak m)$ a nonzero commutative Noetherian local $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with residue field $L=R/\mathfrak m$. Fix $\alpha\in L$, put $k'=k(\alpha)\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension], and let $e=0$ if $\alpha$ is algebraic over $k$ and $e=1$ otherwise [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Form $D=k'\otimes_kR$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the surjection $\epsilon:D\to L$, $a\otimes r\mapsto a\bar r$, and the local ring
$$R'=D_{\ker\epsilon}$$
[def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For any ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ let $I'=IR'$, $A=R/I$ and $A'=R'/I'$, with their induced local structures. Then $R'$ and $A'$ are Noetherian local rings with residue field $L$, and, writing $h_T(n)=\operatorname{length}_T(T/\mathfrak m_T^{n+1})$ and $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length], one has
$$ (\Lambda^e h_A)(n)\le h_{A'}(n)\qquad(n\ge0).$$
If $R$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] and $h_{A'}=\Lambda^e h_A$, then $R'$ is regular local and $\nu^*(R,I)=\nu^*(R',I')$. Here, for a regular local ring $(T,\mathfrak b,\kappa)$ and an ideal $K\subseteq\mathfrak b$, set $E(T,K)=\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak b}T\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak b/K}(T/K))$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]; $\nu^*(T,K)$ lists each $d\ge1$ with multiplicity
$$\dim_\kappa\left(E(T,K)_d\Big/\sum_{j=1}^d(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak b}T)_jE(T,K)_{d-j}\right),$$
sorted increasingly and padded by infinitely many $\infty$'s.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities (1970), (9.1)--(9.6), pp.162--164; Proposition 10, pp.164--165; Proposition 11 and Lemma 12, pp.165--167; residue-extension reduction in Remark (12.2), pp.167--168. Local algebra form, also for a general ideal in a Noetherian local algebra; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: The quotient $A=R/I$ is nonzero local by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure] and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. Its residue field is $L$: the induced quotient $A\to L$ has kernel $\mathfrak m/I$. Choose $u\in R$ with residue $\alpha$ and write $v$ for its image in $A$. Put $S=R[V]_{(\mathfrak m,V)}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak N$, and $C=A[V]_{(\mathfrak m/I,V)}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. By [lem-trf-local-polynomial-tangent-extension], these are Noetherian local rings with residue field $L$, and $S$ is regular when $R$ is regular. The quotient $S/IS$ is canonically $C$: on fractions it sends $f(V)/s(V)$ to $\bar f(V)/\bar s(V)$. A denominator is outside $(\mathfrak m,V)$ exactly when its constant coefficient is outside $\mathfrak m$, a property unchanged modulo $I$; quotienting the fractions therefore gives exactly $C$.

proof.text: We identify the scalar-extension rings explicitly, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, write $k'=k(t)$. Its tensor product with $R$ is $R[t]$ with every nonzero $k[t]$ polynomial inverted: the maps $a(t)\otimes r\mapsto a(t)r$ and $t\mapsto t\otimes1$, $r\mapsto1\otimes r$ are inverse by bilinearity and inversion. The residue map is $t\mapsto\alpha$; its kernel in $R[t]$ becomes $(\mathfrak m,V)$ after $t=V+u$, since reduction sends $V$ to zero. All nonzero $k[t]$ polynomials have nonzero value at $\alpha$, so the final localization is $S$. Thus $R'=S$ and $A'=C$. If $\alpha$ is algebraic, let $p\in k[t]$ be its monic minimal polynomial. Evaluation identifies $k[t]/(p)$ with the field $k(\alpha)$: divide a polynomial by $p$ to compute the kernel; the irreducibility of $p$ gives inverses of nonzero remainder classes by Bezout. Consequently the maps on coefficients and on $t$ identify $k'\otimes_kR$ with $R[t]/(p)$. Let $g(V)=p(V+u)$ in $R[V]$ and let $h$ be its image in $A[V]$. Localizing at the residue kernel gives $R'=S/gS$, $A'=C/hC$. The same fraction formulas give the quotient identifications. Here $g\in\mathfrak N$ and $h\in\mathfrak n$ because $p(\alpha)=0$.

proof.text: It follows from steps 1--2 and [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure, lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] that $R'$ and $A'$ are Noetherian local with residue field $L$ in both cases: their quotient ideals are contained in the maximal ideals of $S$ and $C$, and all residue maps are evaluation at $V=0$ followed by reduction. The quotient $R'/IR'$ is exactly the displayed $A'$.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R$ and $B=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m/I}A$. The new polynomial tangent-cone lemma identifies $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak N}S=G[Z]$ and $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}C=B[Z]$ compatibly with the quotient map. By [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge], all pieces have finite dimension and $h_C(n)=\sum_{r=0}^n\dim_L(B[Z])_r$. Since $(B[Z])_r=\bigoplus_{j=0}^rB_j Z^{r-j}$, rearranging this finite sum gives $h_C(n)=\sum_{a=0}^nh_A(a)=(\Lambda h_A)(n)$. The same bridge applies to $A'$ and to every quotient below. We use the convention $h_C(-1)=0$, so $h_C(n)-h_C(n-1)=h_A(n)$ for every $n\ge0$.

proof.text: In the transcendental case step 2 gives $A'=C$, hence $h_{A'}=\Lambda h_A$ as required for $e=1$. If $R$ is regular then $R'=S$ is regular by step 1. The equality of the standard-degree sequences in this case will follow directly from the polynomial kernel calculation in step 9.

proof.text:
In the algebraic case multiplication by $h\in\mathfrak n$ defines
$$C/\mathfrak n^n\xrightarrow{h}C/\mathfrak n^{n+1}\longrightarrow A'/\mathfrak m_{A'}^{n+1}\longrightarrow0.$$
Its kernel is $K_n=(\mathfrak n^{n+1}:h)/\mathfrak n^n$: this follows by writing out when $ha$ lies in $\mathfrak n^{n+1}$. Its cokernel is $C/(hC+\mathfrak n^{n+1})$, exactly the displayed quotient of $A'$. A module over the quotient $A'$ has the same submodules over $C$ and over $A'$, since all quotient scalars lift, so its two lengths agree by [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to the kernel-image and image-cokernel sequences. All lengths are finite by step 4 and passage to subquotients. We obtain
$$h_C(n)-h_C(n-1)=h_{A'}(n)-\operatorname{length}_C K_n.$$
Step 4 turns this into $h_{A'}(n)=h_A(n)+\operatorname{length}_C K_n\ge h_A(n)$, the desired inequality for $e=0$. At $n=0$, $C/\mathfrak n^0=0$ and $K_0=0$, so the formula also holds there.

proof.text: Still in this equality case, extend the nonzero class of $g$ to an $L$-basis of $\mathfrak N/\mathfrak N^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] this basis has $\dim S$ elements. Choose lifts in $\mathfrak N$; by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] they generate $\mathfrak N$ (a finite $S$-module since $S$ is Noetherian). Thus they form a regular system of parameters, with $g$ first. Step 4 and the equality assumption give $h_{S/IS}=h_C=\Lambda h_A=\Lambda h_{A'}$. Apply [lem-trf-linear-sections-hilbert-standard-degrees] with ambient ring $S$, ideal $IS$, $q=1$ and parameter $g$. Its section quotient is $S/gS=R'$ and the section of $IS$ is $I'$. Its equality clause gives $\nu^*(S,IS)=\nu^*(R',I')$.

proof.text:
For regular $R$, let $E=\ker(G\to B)=E(R,I)$. By the quotient compatibility in [lem-trf-local-polynomial-tangent-extension], the kernel for $S\to S/IS=C$ is $E[Z]\subseteq G[Z]$: a polynomial maps to zero precisely when each coefficient is in $E$. Write $G_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}G_d$ and $P_+=(G[Z])_+$. Since $P_+=(G_+,Z)$, taking the constant coefficient induces the degree-preserving isomorphism
$$E[Z]/P_+E[Z]\simeq E/G_+E.$$
Indeed every term of positive $Z$-degree lies in $ZE[Z]$, and the constant terms of $G_+E[Z]$ are exactly $G_+E$. The degree-$d$ dimensions on the two sides are exactly the multiplicities defining $\nu^*(S,IS)$ and $\nu^*(R,I)$. They agree for every $d\ge1$, so sorting and adding the infinite tails gives equality of these sequences. Combine this with $R'=S$ in step 5 or the section equality of step 8. This proves every asserted equality, including $I=0$ (both kernels vanish and both sequences consist entirely of $\infty$).
